data.cultural_impact: Sheelraj is a culturally significant name in Hindu culture as it is associated with Lord Kubera, who is the Hindu god of wealth. The name suggests the idea of abundance, prosperity, wealth, and good fortune. It also highlights the importance of material prosperity in Hindu belief systems and the belief that gods can bestow wealth and blessings.
data.spiritual_significance: Sheelraj carries a deeper spiritual significance as well. It signifies the idea of being a ruler or a king over one's own material desires and attachments. It encourages the pursuit of wealth and material abundance, but with the understanding that true happiness and spiritual growth come from being a master over these desires, rather than being ruled by them. The name can serve as a reminder of the importance of balancing material success with spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Sheelraj was an influential king of the Vakataka Dynasty in the 4th century AD. He is known to have expanded the kingdom's territories, particularly in the south, and is credited with building several important temples in the region.

Sheelraj was also known as Siladitya, and is mentioned in the inscriptions of the Chalukya King Pulakeshin II in the 7th century AD. He is described as a powerful ruler of the western Karnataka region during the 6th century AD who maintained diplomatic relations with the Chalukyas.
